text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - The British stock market shed half a percent on Monday as political worries and weak futures prices trampled enthusiasm about the multi-billion pound merger between British Telecom and MCI Communications. The FTSE 100 index closed 20.4 points lower at 3,928.1.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse traded down as floor dealings caught up with losses made during late Friday electronic dealings. Weaker German bonds also weighed on the market. The DAX index of 30 leading shares ended down 11.39 points, or 0.42 percent, at 2,671.86. In post bourse trade the DAX was up 8.54 at 2,678.73.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended higher in slow trade and light volume as the market grew cautious ahead of U.S. presidential and congressional elections on Tuesday. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) gained 13.1 points, or 0.35 percent, to 3,749.2 points. The Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 6.42 points, or 0.27 percent, at 2,409.13 points. TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed for a holiday on Monday, but trading will resume on Tuesday. On Friday, the key Nikkei 225 index rose 166.20 points, or 0.81 percent, to 20,633,06. December futures finished 180 points up at 20,640.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng index managed to eke out a new closing high, aided by a jump in New World Development shares ahead of the release of the company's results this week. The index closed 30.13 points higher at 12,559.40. Turnover was HK$6.34 billion, compared with HK$7.3 billion on Friday.

SYDNEY - Hopes of an interest rate cut hoisted Australian shares higher by the close although trade remained lacklustre as players awaited the result of the Reserve Bank's deliberations on Tuesday. The All Ordinaries index rose 18.1 points to 2357.5.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares dipped as a late wave of futures-related selling hit the index and caused it to finish at its day lows. The all-share index dropped 18.5 points to end at 6,952.9 as industrials fell 18.8 points to 8,175.3.
Golds did better as shares firmed on a steadier bullion price, although it was still below the important $380 an ounce level. The golds index ended up 9.9 points at 1,732.4.
